item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to high-level dialogue marking 5th anniversary of GDI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has sent a congratulatory letter to a high-level dialogue marking the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) held at the UN headquarters in New York on Friday. Development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting the well-being of humankind, Xi said. Xi recalled that he proposed the GDI at the UN General Assembly five years ago to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, the GDI has been widely implemented, with cooperation projects under the initiative taking root and yielding outcomes in more than 120 countries, writing a new chapter of common development and win-win cooperation, Xi noted. Xi pointed out that nowadays, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and people in all countries are more keen about development. As the world's largest developing country and a member of the Global South, China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy, advance the GDI, turn the vision of the sustainable development goals into reality, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said. ■

item.title: China, U.S. agree on constructive strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan have a chat over tea with U.S. President Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) WASHINGTON, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. The consensus was reached during a tea chat at the White House attended by Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, and Trump and his wife, Melania Trump. Xi said the trip to Washington was his first state visit to the United States in 11 years. During the visit, the two sides added new substance to the vision for the China-U.S. relationship, and agreed to jointly build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Xi said. The two sides also achieved mutually beneficial outcomes in the economic and trade fields, which will be welcomed by the people of both countries and the international community, he added. Stressing that the future of China-U.S. relations is bright, Xi said that it reflects the trend of history. The road to a bright future is often winding, with difficulties and challenges bound to arise along the way, Xi said, adding that it is in line with the laws governing the development of things. Xi said he is willing to work with Trump to write a new chapter in the history of China-U.S. relations with the courage and a sense of responsibility to history. Calling Xi's state visit to the United States constructive and very successful, Trump said that the two sides held in-depth exchanges on U.S.-China relations and major international and regional issues, achieving positive outcomes that will benefit both countries. He said he looks forward to maintaining close contact with Xi and jointly guiding the development of U.S.-China relations. After the tea chat, Xi and Peng, accompanied by Trump and Melania, visited the U.S. National Archives. They walked together into the central hall, where they were briefed on the National Archives and its exhibits. The archives carry the wisdom of the forebears and offer insights for the future, Xi said, adding that over the past 250 years, the American people have pursued the American Dream and built a prosperous country and a beautiful home on the North American continent. The Chinese people, inheriting 5,000 years of Chinese civilization, have continued to make new achievements on the new journey toward realizing the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi said. As two distinctive countries, China and the United States have different histories and cultures, social systems and development paths, Xi said. However, the people of the two countries share the same aspiration for a better life despite the differences, he said. If the two countries recognize and respect their differences, deepen mutual understanding and learn from each other, seek the biggest common denominator, expand the list of areas for cooperation, and properly manage differences, China-U.S. relations will enjoy steady and sustained growth, Xi said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, together with U.S. President Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump, pose for a group photo at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 25, 2026. item.title: Seven golds on debut: Zhang Zhanshuo makes Asian Games history
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
TOKYO, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- Moments after touching the wall in the men's 400m freestyle final on Friday, Zhang Zhanshuo surfaced, raised both hands and slowly counted from one to seven. The 19-year-old Chinese swimmer had just completed his first Asian Games with seven gold medals. The Tokyo Aquatics Center was filled with cheers. Zhang, however, appeared remarkably calm. "I feel much calmer than I had imagined," Zhang said after winning the 400m freestyle in an Asian Games record of 3 minutes 41.28 seconds. "Of course, I'm very happy to win these seven gold medals, and I will turn them into greater motivation going forward." The victory made Zhang the first swimmer to win seven gold medals at a single edition of the Asian Games. More significantly, his haul equaled the Games record for most gold medals won by an athlete at a single edition, a mark set by DPRK shooter So Gil-san in 1982. For Chinese swimming, it was also a new benchmark, as Zhang surpassed the six-gold haul of teammate Zhang Yufei at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023. His seven titles came from a demanding mix of individual and relay events: the men's 200m, 400m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle, the men's 4x100m and 4x200m freestyle relays, and the mixed 4x100m medley relay. He won gold in seven of the eight events he entered, while setting an Asian record in the 200m freestyle, Games records in the 400m and 800m, and Asian records in the two men's freestyle relays. But the seven medals did not change the way Zhang viewed the competition. Asked what had excited him most during the Games, he did not point to the medal ceremonies or the seven-gold haul. Instead, he recalled the instant he touched the wall. "When I touched the wall and came out of the water, I looked back at the big screen and saw my time flashing, or the 'AR' mark," he said. Then came the quiet count from one to seven. "It was a perfect finish to the Games," Zhang said. The calmness was not a sign that Zhang considered his work finished. Quite the opposite, when asked about his ambitions for the Los Angeles Olympics, Zhang stressed that the Asian Games was not his ultimate goal. "I need to settle down and face the gaps between myself and the world's best. The Asian Games is not my ultimate goal," he said. And his next target is the world record. Zhang's 3:41.28 was just 1.25 seconds outside the world record, and he said breaking that mark would be one of his next goals over the coming two years. "I think that will be one of my next goals, and I will give my all to chase the world record," he said. The young swimmer is also clear about what stands between him and that target. "There are many things I need to improve," Zhang said. "That's also one of the purposes of this competition, to make a new summary and find the gaps, both technically and in terms of ability." Zhang said his turning technique still lagged behind that of some of the world's top swimmers, making it an important focus for his next phase of training. The same approach applies to his events. Rather than picking one as his favorite, Zhang said he wanted to continue developing across the middle and long distance free events. "Everything is possible. I will stay humble and keep pushing forward," he said. At 19, Zhang has already matched a record that had stood for more than four decades. He left the Tokyo Aquatics Center with seven gold medals, but also with a clear sense that there was more work to do. Asked to rate his performance at the Games, Zhang gave himself 85 out of 100. For Zhang, the number seven therefore marks both an achievement and a starting point. "There are still gaps between me and the world level in some events," he said. "I will turn these gold medals into greater motivation." ■

item.title: Digital trade, AI inject new momentum into China-Africa ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
HANGZHOU, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- As the digital economy accelerates, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a new growth driver for China-Africa economic and trade cooperation, driven by expanding practical applications, according to a new report. Titled China-Africa Economic and Trade Cooperation: Progress and Outlook 2026, the report was unveiled at the ongoing fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, the capital of east China's Zhejiang Province. The expo, an event dedicated to promoting digital trade and industrial cooperation, is being held from Sept. 23 to 27. This year, the number of its overseas pavilions has already exceeded the combined total of all previous editions. The application of AI is shifting from a future option to a real agenda in China-Africa cooperation, the report found. This shift is characterized by strong application-scenario drives. Cooperation has expanded into areas such as disaster prevention, healthcare, smart agriculture and urban governance. "Increasingly, it will require digital infrastructure that enables African businesses to compete in a rapidly changing global economy," said Klaus-Dieter Kaempfer, chief executive of Absa China, noting that digital trade has the potential to lower barriers to entry, connect businesses to new markets and enable entrepreneurs to participate in global commerce regardless of geography. Alhaji Sarjoh Bah, permanent representative of the African Union to China, called for deeper cooperation in five areas: trade facilitation and cross-border e-commerce; interoperable payments; trusted data governance, cybersecurity and dispute prevention; digital intelligence and industrial parks for value addition; and people-to-people exchanges and digital talent. Bah called for linking Chinese digital trade industrial parks with African special economic zones and industrial parks, and combining cloud computing, data centers, smart logistics and AI with manufacturing and processing. "Africa seeks to move from exporting raw minerals to producing processed goods. It seeks equally to move from generating raw data to producing processed intelligence," said Bah, stressing the need for local content, skills development and technology transfer, and building AI systems that reflect African languages and realities. Concrete cooperation projects are already underway. A highlight of the event was the promotion of the "Mazu" intelligent weather warning system. Designed to meet Africa's needs for meteorological disaster prevention, the system has been deployed in Ethiopia and Djibouti, offering targeted services. The deepening digital ties mirror the robust growth in China-Africa trade. In 2025, China-Africa trade grew by 17.7 percent year on year to reach 348 billion U.S. dollars. On May 1, China fully implemented a zero-tariff treatment for 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations. China's digitally deliverable service trade value expanded at an average annual rate of 11.2 percent between 2016 and 2025, outpacing the global average by 1.8 percentage points. ■

item.title: Xi-Trump summit provides new strategic guidance for China-U.S. ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
* Chinese President Xi Jinping engaged intensively on Thursday with his host, U.S. President Donald Trump, at the White House during his state visit to the United States, reaching common understanding on many issues. * Xi's visit comes less than half a year after Trump's state visit to China in May, when the two presidents agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. * While China and the United States compete in AI, they have even more reasons to cooperate, Xi said, urging the two major countries in AI to leverage respective strengths rather than guard against each other. * At the state dinner, both presidents looked back on the long history of exchanges between the Chinese and American peoples, underscoring the importance of people-to-people ties. WASHINGTON, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- From a welcome ceremony and a formal meeting to a state dinner, Chinese President Xi Jinping engaged intensively on Thursday with his host, U.S. President Donald Trump, at the White House during his state visit to the United States. The two leaders conducted sincere and in-depth exchanges and reached common understanding on many issues, which has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and provided new strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations. PUTTING VISION INTO ACTION "I am ready to work with you to steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relationship on a steady course toward the future," Xi said at the welcome ceremony at the White House. Xi's visit comes less than half a year after Trump's state visit to China in May, when the two presidents agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Later at his White House meeting with Trump, Xi called for translating that vision into action and finding the right way for the two major countries to get along with each other. The two sides need to work toward a relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences, and promises of peace, Xi said. Xi noted that China and the United States should, and fully can, achieve mutual benefit and win-win results through practical cooperation, help each other succeed through healthy competition, properly manage differences by seeking common ground while respecting differences, and build peace by fostering mutual trust, so that a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability can better benefit the two peoples and people around the world. Trump, for his part, said he and Xi are good friends who have maintained in-depth and close communication, and expressed confidence that U.S.-China relations would be handled well under the leadership of the two heads of state. The meticulous arrangements for Xi's state visit, down to the details and with care and consideration, reflected the importance Trump attached to Xi's trip. After receiving Xi in person at the airport one day earlier, Trump hosted the grand welcome ceremony at the White House. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, watched a performance by the United States Marines in the company of the U.S. presidential couple. The ceremony also featured a military review, with U.S. honor guards from different military services performing traditional drills and playing instrumental music. Multiple combat aircraft flew over the White House in honor of the Chinese and U.S. presidents and their wives. Following the talks, the two presidential couples met again for the state dinner. Inside, red blossoms and red linens decorated the room, a choice a White House release said reflected the color's longstanding cultural significance in China. "In less than half a year, the Chinese and American presidents have exchanged state visits, making history in our bilateral engagement," Xi said at the state dinner hosted by Trump. The strongest signal to the world is that the leaders of the world's two most consequential major countries, though overtly competitive, can meet in harmony and with good spirit, which is the headline achievement, commented U.S. scholar Robert Lawrence Kuhn. COOPERATION GOES BOTH WAYS From Beijing in May to Washington in September, practical cooperation has remained high on the agenda of China-U.S. interactions. At the ceremony, Xi called on the two countries to "cooperate with sincerity." Xi said the two sides share "deeply intertwined" interests and ample room for cooperation, noting that China-U.S. collaboration "may not solve every problem in the world," but many would be hard to resolve without it. During his talks with Trump, Xi said the latest round of trade and economic consultations between the two countries had produced a new joint arrangement, calling it good news for industries and people of both countries, as well as the global economy. Noting that cooperation is a two-way street, Xi said as long as the two sides uphold the spirit of equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit, they can find a way out of problems. The state dinner offered another glimpse of the breadth of economic ties between the two countries. Executives from major U.S. aviation, technology and financial firms were among the guests, including some who had accompanied Trump to Beijing in May, such as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk. Artificial intelligence (AI) was another area discussed by the two leaders. While China and the United States compete in AI, they have even more reasons to cooperate, Xi said, urging the two major countries in AI to leverage respective strengths rather than guard against each other. The two sides should keep AI under human control, uphold a human-centered approach and use AI for good, ensuring that it serves human progress, Xi added. Trump also stressed the importance of maintaining dialogue on AI, calling it the technology that bears on the future of humanity. CARRYING ON FRIENDSHIP At the state dinner, both presidents looked back on the long history of exchanges between the Chinese and American peoples, underscoring the importance of people-to-people ties. Xi recalled how the two peoples stood shoulder to shoulder in the fight against Japanese militarist aggression more than 80 years ago, and how Ping-Pong Diplomacy reopened the door to bilateral exchanges more than half a century ago. He also recounted the story of American Ronald Sakolsky, who supported Chinese desert control worker Yin Yuzhen's tree-planting efforts more than 20 years ago, calling it a shining example of friendly exchanges between the two peoples. Such exchanges, Xi said, have promoted heart-to-heart communication between our peoples and strengthened public support for China-U.S. friendship and cooperation. Trump, meanwhile, reviewed the long history of U.S.-China exchanges, pointing to early commercial ties and the exchange of "goods, knowledge, customs and ideas." "As the leaders of our two nations, President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better," Trump said. New steps are now being taken to carry that friendship forward. At the welcome ceremony, Xi announced that two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will soon arrive at Zoo Atlanta and meet the American people. He also invited 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchange and study programs over the next five years. "The hope of the China-U.S. relationship lies in our people, and its future lies with the young," Xi said. In 2023, during his visit to San Francisco, Xi announced a similar initiative inviting 50,000 young Americans to China over five years. That target has already been achieved. "President Xi announced that he wants to double the number of students over the next five years. That's very positive, very significant, because I believe that those kinds of exchanges and students going back and forth are very, very important," said Kenneth Quinn, president emeritus of the World Food Prize Foundation. ■

item.title: Volume I of "China's Governance Under Xi Jinping's Leadership" presented at Jordan book fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
AMMAN, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- A promotional event for the first volume of "China's Governance Under Xi Jinping's Leadership," compiled by Xinhua News Agency, was held on Thursday at the 25th Amman International Book Fair in Jordan's capital. Jamal Dmour, head of the Jordanian-Chinese Friendship Society, introduced the new book to the audience at the event, saying that China's remarkable development experience offers valuable insights for the advancement of humanity. Speaking at the event, Gong Anmin, the charge d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Jordan, said the first volume offers a panoramic media perspective on China's development since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC), documenting the practice of the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core in advancing the cause of building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation. Gong said the book provides an important window for the world to explore the keys to China's success in pursuing Chinese modernization. The first volume of "China's Governance Under Xi Jinping's Leadership" contains 26 feature stories and 41 news photographs by Xinhua, offering a vivid, multimedia account of the great practice of China advancing under the leadership of Xi, and fully demonstrating the powerful truth and practical force of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The 25th Amman International Book Fair attracted more than 400 publishing houses from over 20 countries. ■
